newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia aircraft firm signs deal to build jets.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia aircraft firm signs deal to build jets.

text.p: Indonesian state-owned aircraft maker PT Industri Pesawat Terbang Nusantara (IPTN) signed an agreement on Tuesday with private firm PT Dua Satu Tiga Puluh (DSTP) to finance a project to build jet airliners.
The agreement was signed by Research and Technology Minister Jusuf Habibie, who also heads IPTN, and DSTP president-director Saadilah Mursid, who is also the Cabinet Secretary.
Habibie said the 100-seater version of the N-2130 would cost $20.5 million and the 130-seater $26.65 million.
President Suharto, who is president-commissioner of DSTP, had encouraged Indonesians to finance the project. DSTP was set up specifically to finance the plane project.
DSTP has raised one trillion rupiah by selling 400,000 shares worth $1,000 each, Mursid told reporters. He said only Indonesians and local firms could buy DSTP shares.
He said N-2130 project needed $2 billion to meet engineering, development and certification costs.
Habibie said the world would need 3,790 100-seater passenger planes between 2005 and 2025.
"We are convinced the N-2130 will be able to grab a 25-percent market share because the design and technology are new," Habibie told reporters after the signing.
He said the first of the planes would enter the market in 2006. The IPTN-made N-250 turboprop passenger plane, the first locally made model, had its maiden flight in August last year.
